## What was wrong

`MultiframeWrapper` (Enhanced MR / Supplement 49) built its affine from the wrong frames. The archived acquisition stores its 112 frames in **descending** `InStackPositionNumber` (frame 0 = in-stack 56 at *y* = +35.5 mm), which DICOM explicitly permits — C.7.6.17: "the actual order of the Frames in the object is up to the generating application".

- `get_data()` correctly ordered planes by `DimensionIndexValues` (in-stack ascending, running toward +*y*).
- `image_position` took `frames[0]` — the *last* plane of that block.
- `slice_normal` came from the `ImageOrientationPatient` cross product alone (0, −1, 0), i.e. against the direction the data planes actually advance.

The affine therefore described the volume back-to-front and offset by the full stack length: every one of the 112 frames was placed at the wrong patient position, giving RMS radius 74.891 mm instead of 72.354 mm.

## The fix (`source/nibabel/nicom/dicomwrappers.py`, only file touched)

- **`frame_order`** — new cached property holding the dimension-index sort. `get_data()` now uses it, so plane ordering and geometry come from one source of truth.
- **`image_position`** — when position is per-frame, uses the frame giving the *first* data plane (`frame_order[0]`), not the first frame stored.
- **`slice_normal`** — override that keeps the IOP-derived plane normal but takes its *sign* from the `ImagePositionPatient` travel across the planes of the block, so the third affine column follows the data.
- Fallbacks (`_first_frame_no`, `_slice_frame_positions`, `_order_errors`) preserve legacy behaviour when a file carries no usable frame ordering or per-frame positions, and `get_data` gained a reshape guard so single-frame files (pydicom returns a 2-D `pixel_array`) no longer crash. Nothing acquisition-specific is encoded; `voxel_sizes`, `image_shape`, scaling, StackID and derived-DWI handling are untouched.
